title: Failure triage
description: One agent's decision about what a stage failure means and what happens next. Written by the failure-triage agent after reading the failed run's complete log — which nothing running inside that run can see.

diagnosis.description: What broke and why, traced to a line, a limit or an outage — not which step went red.

evidence.description: The log line, file:line or command output the diagnosis rests on.

verdict.description: rerun: transient, same stage unchanged. resume: the work survived, continue from where it stopped. repair: a defect in the project's code, inside the current work order. replan: the plan cannot be built as described. wait: an outage or a rate or quota limit — the stage parks and runs again after a cooldown. escalate: a person is needed.

confidence.description: How sure the diagnosis is. A low score with a named uncertainty is worth more than a high one that rests on an unread log.

transient.description: Required true for a `rerun` verdict: nothing about the repository changed, so only a genuinely transient cause makes the next run different.

framework_defect.description: A defect in the pipeline itself. Never applied by triage: plumbing goes to the bounded self-fix stage (lib/self-fix.js decides from `file`), a rule or a prompt to a person.

file.description: The exact path of the file that is wrong, e.g. .sdlc/bin/lib/actions.js — it decides whether the pipeline may fix it itself.

survived.description: For a `resume` verdict: what work already exists and where — a pushed branch, an open PR, a stashed plan on the ledger.
